turns.narration:
*Nicco moves away from the public auction area, skirting the edge of the crowd. Beyond the pens and the clerk tables, the square gives way to a row of less prominent setups — canvases stretched over wooden frames, rented stalls, a few permanent-looking storefronts set back from the main traffic. Hand-lettered signs and display arrangements distinguish these from the public auction: smaller groups, sometimes only one or two people at a time, with a seller or agent attending directly. Buyers here speak in lower voices, take longer looking.*

*The first stall he passes has a heavyset woman seated on a stool beside two young men who stand quietly under a rope line. She glances up at Nicco, measures him with a look, then goes back to watching the passing traffic. A few stalls down, a man with a hooked nose and large, roughened hands is wiping down a ledger on a narrow table outside a canvas enclosure, a single figure sitting behind him on a low bench.*

*The strip of private sellers extends along the back edge of the square, mixed with caravan supply tents and a few closed doors that might lead to more permanent arrangements. The traffic thins here compared to the auction crowd, and the fog muffles the noise from the main square.*

*Nicco continues along the back edge of the square. The stalls thin out further, spaced wider apart where the packed earth gives way to gravel and the fog thickens against the outer wall. A few canvases are pulled shut with no one in attendance. One stall displays three people standing in a loose line beside a chalkboard scrawled with abbreviated notes — a woman with grey-streaked hair pinned up under a cloth sits on a crate nearby, splitting her attention between a steaming cup and a pair of buyers already inspecting the nearest figure. She doesn't look up as Nicco passes.*

*Further along, a permanent storefront set back from the row has its door propped open with a stone. A wooden frame supports a faded awning, and through the dim interior Nicco can make out the shapes of benches and a counter. No one stands outside. A hand-lettered board nailed to the frame reads in plain letters what might be a name or a trade marker, but the paint has worn too thin to read clearly from the path.*

*Beyond that, the row peters out where caravan supply tents crowd together — rope, feed sacks, harness fittings — and the market's slave-trading edge gives way to ordinary livestock and freight handling. The fog sits low and the foot traffic here is mostly handlers and teamsters paying him no attention. Whatever private sellers work this stretch, Nicco has reached the end of them.*
